title: LLM Performance Predictors: Learning When to Escalate in Hybrid Human-AI Moderation Systems
venue: Proc. of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2026)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of deciding when large language model (LLM) outputs can be trusted in hybrid human-AI moderation workflows and when they should be escalated to human reviewers. The authors frame this as an uncertainty quantification and cost-sensitive selective classification problem: the system must balance the cost of allowing an incorrect automated decision through against the cost of human review.

The proposed approach is a supervised meta-model built from "LLM Performance Predictors" (LPPs), which combine gray-box signals such as token-level log-probabilities, entropy, and margin-based measures with black-box signals such as verbalized confidence and uncertainty-attribution indicators. These indicators are designed to distinguish evidence deficits from policy gaps, enabling different escalation paths for ambiguous cases versus cases that may require policy revision or retraining. The method uses ridge regression plus calibration to estimate whether the base LLM is correct, and then applies a threshold-based routing policy to either trust the LLM or escalate to humans.

The empirical evaluation is in content moderation, not education. The paper tests multiple proprietary and open-source LLMs on two moderation datasets: an English text moderation dataset and a multimodal, multilingual video moderation dataset. Results show that the LPP meta-model generally improves error-prediction performance and reduces expected cost compared with standard uncertainty baselines such as maximum softmax probability, entropy, and top-2 margin. The authors also report that chain-of-thought prompting inflated confidence and harmed calibration in this setting. Overall, the paper concludes that uncertainty-aware routing can make human-AI moderation more efficient and explainable, but it also notes limitations around labeled-data requirements, domain shift, and model-specific variability.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed conference paper with a clear empirical evaluation, but it is not an education study and lacks K-12 relevance, randomization, or direct learner outcomes. The evidence is primarily technical/observational and applies to moderation workflows rather than instructional settings.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no demonstrated impact on K-12 learning or teacher practice; the paper addresses content moderation operations. Any relevance to Khanmigo-like tutoring is indirect, via uncertainty routing and escalation rather than student-facing educational effects.

interventions.use_case: supervised uncertainty estimation and selective escalation for LLM-based content moderation, using LPP features to decide when to trust the model versus route to human review

finding.finding_summary: The paper finds that the LPP meta-model reduces expected moderation cost and human escalations relative to standard uncertainty baselines across multiple LLMs. On the OpenAI Moderation dataset, expected cost falls from $132 to $38 for gpt-4o-mini (71% reduction) with escalations dropping from 331 to 148; on the multimodal dataset, cost falls from $37 to $22 for gpt-4o-mini and from $51 to $40 for gemini-2.5-flash-lite, indicating more targeted human review.
finding.measure: Expected cost ($), escalation count, escalation ratio in selective moderation routing

finding.finding_summary: The paper’s main contribution is a human-AI routing framework for production moderation workflows that aims to improve reliability, scalability, and explainability of LLM deployment. It reports that uncertainty attribution can distinguish evidence deficits from policy gaps, supporting workflow actions such as escalation to senior reviewers or policy updates/active learning cycles, though these are not educational outcomes.
finding.measure: Error prediction performance and routing decisions intended to improve moderation workflow governance
